title: Visible Light
summary: Light as radiation, the visible spectrum, how light travels, reflection, refraction, absorption and why objects have colour.

notes.text: Light is a form of **radiation**: energy that travels as waves and needs no medium, so it can cross the vacuum of space. Light travels at about **300 000 km per second**, the fastest speed in the universe. Objects that give off their own light are **luminous** (the sun, a candle flame, a light bulb); objects we see because they reflect light are **non-luminous** (the moon, a book, you).

White light is a mixture of colours. When white light passes through a triangular glass **prism**, it splits into a band of colours called the **visible spectrum**. This splitting is called **dispersion**. A rainbow forms in the same way when sunlight passes through raindrops.

notes.label: Memory aid
notes.text: **ROY G BIV**: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet.
Light travels in **straight lines**, drawn as rays with arrows. This is why shadows form: an opaque object blocks the light and leaves a dark area behind it.

rows: Almost all light passes through; you can see clearly through it
Some light passes through but is scattered; you cannot see clearly
No light passes through; light is absorbed or reflected

notes.text: When light bounces off a surface it is **reflected**. A smooth, shiny surface (a mirror) gives **regular reflection** and a clear image. A rough surface (paper) gives **diffuse reflection**, scattering light in all directions.

notes.caption: The law of reflection (both angles measured from the normal)

notes.caption: The angle of incidence (i) equals the angle of reflection (r)

notes.title: The law of reflection
notes.problem: A ray of light strikes a flat mirror at an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
steps: The law of reflection says the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Both angles are measured from the normal, the line at 90° to the mirror.

notes.text: **Refraction** is the bending of light when it passes from one transparent medium to another, because light changes speed. Light slows down and bends **towards the normal** when it enters a denser medium (air into water or glass) and bends **away from the normal** when it leaves.

items: A straw in a glass of water looks bent at the surface.
A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is.
Lenses in spectacles, cameras and the eye refract light to focus an image.

notes.text: When light falls on an opaque object, some colours are **absorbed** and others are **reflected**. The colour we see is the colour that is reflected into our eyes.

rows: All colours (so it heats up most in the sun)
Mostly red and blue (used for photosynthesis)

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: A red object seen in green light looks **black**, because there is no red light for it to reflect and it absorbs the green.

notes.title: A red shirt in green light
notes.problem: Why does a red shirt look red in sunlight but almost black under pure green light?
steps: White sunlight contains all colours. The shirt reflects red and absorbs the rest.
Green light contains no red for the shirt to reflect.
The shirt absorbs the green, so almost no light reaches your eyes.
notes.answer: It reflects only red, and there is no red in green light.

✓ Light travels in straight lines (1)
✓ An opaque object blocks the light, leaving a dark area behind it where light cannot reach (1)

questions.prompt: What colour does a red cap appear in green light? Explain.
questions.memo:
✓ Black (1)
✓ It absorbs the green light and there is no red light for it to reflect (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why a pencil in a glass of water appears bent.
questions.memo:
✓ Light from the pencil changes speed when it passes from water into air (1)
✓ so it bends (refracts) and the pencil appears to be in a different position (1)
